title: What bit me along the way
headSub: The build was not smooth. Four operational problems taught me the most, and each looked fine right up until it did not.
head: Where
The challenge
What fixed it

cells.text: the cost dashboard read three times under the real bill for weeks, while every test stayed green
an invariant that follows the value across layers, not a per-layer unit test
a settings dropdown left the busiest agent on the expensive model; the bill climbed quietly for days
cost caps enforced in code in three places, never a dashboard you watch after the fact
scoring ran one job at a time, about 75 seconds a run
concurrency on independent calls, about 20 seconds at the same cost, with a timing test to guard it
two of the three lethal-trifecta legs are open by necessity, and the model is a black box I cannot inspect
hold the third leg nearly shut: no tools, no egress, a human on anything irreversible

takeaway.text: Every one of these looked fine until it did not. {{amber:The dashboard stayed green while the numbers under it were wrong.}} The fixes were architecture, not paying more attention.
